paper_style.palette_strategy: Categorical method palette reused across all result plots: UP red, KT blue, DtACI green, SFOGD yellow, P Ctrl purple, PI Ctrl cyan; black/gray are reserved for ground truth, ideal calibration, target, and tolerance references. Method identity is almost always color-only.
paper_style.vector_raster_mix: PDF has no embedded raster images in pdfimages inspection; plots, axes, and table rules are vector PDF objects, while the audit used 200 dpi raster renderings for visual inspection. Plot text includes Type3 ArialMT/DejaVuSans objects alongside Computer Modern document text.
paper_style.style_consistency: The appendix repeats stable plot templates, palette, grid, legend placement, and booktabs tables. Consistency is strong across datasets, but caption self-containment and panel-key detail are weak in the repeated “As in Figure …” series.

figures.evidence_relation: The headline claim that UP-OCP has the best size–coverage trade-off is routed from the AXP results paragraph to this frontier, then qualified by Table 1 and expanded by Appendix Figures 11–13 and Table 2.
design_strengths: Single page-width frontier makes the two-objective trade-off immediately comparable.
Method colors and circular points make the 50 target levels traceable along each trajectory.

Color is the only method key, so print/grayscale readers lose method identity.

cross_object_system.visual_narrative: The visual sequence moves from the AXP headline frontier (Figure 1), calibration (Figure 2), one dynamics illustration (Figure 3), and replicated summary (Figure 4), then expands into diagnostics, local-adaptivity panels, distributional Pareto slices, tables, and explicit failure cases (Figures 78–80).
cross_object_system.caption_system: Captions are short, serif document captions. Main figures state the objective or setting; most appendix captions name only dataset/metric, and repeated panels use “As in Figure …”, which saves space but weakens standalone interpretation. Failure captions are the most informative because they state the observed mechanism and consequence.
cross_object_system.table_header_system: All tables use one header row with a left metric column and method columns. The metric vocabulary is stable across real datasets; synthetic tables omit the longest-error row, so row schemas are not fully uniform. Booktabs rules and bold highlights are reused, with no uncertainty headers.
cross_object_system.method_result_ablation_link: UP-OCP is the red reference method throughout. Local panels compare it with one baseline at a time; aggregate tables and target-level frontiers then summarize the same comparison. Figures 78–80 act as stress/failure cases for learning-rate/controller assumptions rather than formal ablations.
cross_object_system.main_appendix_link: The appendix is a systematic expansion of the four main result objects: Table 2 and Figures 11–14 deepen AXP; Figures 15–77 repeat the local/quantile/calibration grammar across AAPL, AMZN, GOOGL, electricity, and synthetic settings; Figures 78–80 expose failure modes.
cross_object_system.typography_consistency: Computer Modern document text and tables are stable; plot interiors use embedded ArialMT/DejaVuSans Type3 objects at roughly 6–10 pt. The visual language is coherent, but small legends and axes are near the lower readable limit in dense appendix pages.
cross_object_system.color_consistency: Method colors are highly consistent across all result objects and baseline panels. The lack of redundant line/marker encoding makes the system less robust to grayscale and color-vision limitations; black/gray references provide redundancy only for calibration targets.
